verdict.rationale: USCIS documents public APIs on its Torch developer platform (Case Status API and FOIA Request and Status). It also documents a clear key-issuance path: register a developer account, build in a sandbox, then pass a demo to receive production keys. The evidence never states rate limits, and the APIs are described only at a summary level, not as concrete published endpoint paths. Missing for 10: stated rate limits, explicit endpoint paths or reference documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the service documents a public API for its data — published endpoints, a key-issuance path, and stated rate limits on its own pages

citations.quote: Case Status API: Provides case status information to USCIS customers and their representatives who require regular access to case status information.
This API allows consumers to create a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) or Privacy Act (PA) request, for Alien File material, about or on behalf of the subject of record.
Complete the onboarding task to register for a USCIS Torch API Developer account.
Gain Access and develop in our Sandbox environment to send test data.
Pass the demo and receive production keys to launch your application.
